app_recommendations: Differentiate cooking logic by pork cut collagen content: strictly enforce 145°F (62.8°C) with a 3-minute rest for lean cuts (tenderloin, loin chops) to keep them juicy and pink, while directing collagen-rich cuts (shoulder, ribs, belly) to 195°F–205°F slow braises/roasts.
For pork tenderloin, mandate silverskin removal in the prep instructions to eliminate tough chewing.

For crispy-skin roasts (shoulder, belly), implement the two-phase temperature sequence: low slow roast (320°F–325°F) for 2 to 2.5 hours, followed by a high-heat blast (450°F–485°F) for 25 to 30 minutes to blister the crackling.
For rib preparations, instruct users to strip the underside membrane before applying rubs to guarantee tenderness and spice penetration.
